topics.topic: Which backup first contains an import committed after the next daily snapshot begins
questions: If the import commits during the next daily run but after that run's snapshot began, does "the next daily run" contain the import, or does only a later run contain it?
If the import commits during the next daily run but after that run's snapshot began, must that run contain the import, or is the import first contained in the following backup?

quotes: It reaches the backups with the next daily run (A18).
A change committed after the snapshot began is not in this backup, which holds the store as its snapshot saw it; a later backup holds whatever the store holds when its own snapshot is taken.
judgement.why: A16 requires the next daily run to carry the import, while A18 excludes it when that run's snapshot began before the import committed.

bases.passage: It reaches the backups with the next daily run (A18).
A change committed after the snapshot began is not in this backup, which holds the store as its snapshot saw it; a later backup holds whatever the store holds when its own snapshot is taken.

unsupported_sides: It reaches the backups with the next daily run (A18).
A change committed after the snapshot began is not in this backup, which holds the store as its snapshot saw it; a later backup holds whatever the store holds when its own snapshot is taken.

witness.initial: The migration closure is absent, and the next daily backup has begun its store snapshot.
events: Registry starts the daily backup snapshot.
The owner confirms the import, whose transaction commits after that snapshot began.
After a store loss, the owner puts that backup in place and starts Registry.
outcomes: Under A16 rule 10, the restored backup contains the imported projects, Customers and migration closure because it came from the next daily run.
Under A18 rule 1, the restored backup excludes the import because it committed after the snapshot began.
witness.observer: The owner and callers of the restored Registry
basis: An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers, the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry (M09) in one transaction.

A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs: one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot, the instant being when its read transaction began.
It has no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its place on the host, outside Registry (Explicit exclusions), and Registry starts on it as on any store.

provenance.quote: It has no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its place on the host, outside Registry

topics.topic: Concurrency locking, ordering, and wait policy for backup readers and writers
questions: Which store locking/journal mode, lock-acquisition order and wait policy define how the engine orders a concurrent backup reader and writer, including whether the reader or writer proceeds first and how an otherwise busy operation waits without failing?

quotes: A write and the copy may wait for each other only as the store's engine orders a reader and the writer; neither is refused or fails for the other.
judgement.divergence: The backup reader may proceed first, delaying the write and excluding it, or the writer may proceed first, delaying the backup and including the write; the owner notices the latency and the contents of a restored backup.
judgement.why: The rule delegates observable ordering and waiting behaviour to the store engine without fixing that engine behaviour.

witness.initial: Registry is running at 03:00 UTC with a writable store, no backup run active and an owner write ready to commit.
events: The daily backup attempts to establish its snapshot while the owner write attempts to commit.
The backup completes and is kept.
After a store loss, the owner puts that backup in place and starts Registry.
outcomes: The reader proceeds first, the write waits, and the restored backup excludes the write.
The writer proceeds first, the backup waits, and the restored backup includes the write.
basis: Every day at 03:00 UTC, while Registry runs with its service tokens, it makes one backup run; a 03:00 that finds Registry stopped, or in an owner-only start (rule 9), makes no run, and none is made later in its place.
A write and the copy may wait for each other only as the store's engine orders a reader and the writer; neither is refused or fails for the other.
It has no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its place on the host, outside Registry (Explicit exclusions), and Registry starts on it as on any store.

provenance.quote: It has no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its place on the host, outside Registry

topics.topic: Exact event establishing a backup snapshot and the sequence number recorded
questions: If a write commits after the backup transaction is opened but before its first snapshot-establishing read, is that write included, and which instant and last sequence number must the backup record?

quotes: A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs: one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot, the instant being when its read transaction began.
A change committed after the snapshot began is not in this backup, which holds the store as its snapshot saw it; a later backup holds whatever the store holds when its own snapshot is taken.
judgement.divergence: The snapshot may be fixed when the read transaction begins, excluding audit entry 21 and recording sequence 20, or on its first snapshot-establishing read, including entry 21 and recording sequence 21; the owner sees the difference in backup metadata and after restoration.
judgement.why: The text fixes the recorded instant at transaction start but does not identify whether the snapshot itself is established then or by a later engine read.

witness.initial: The store's last audit sequence number is 20, and no backup run is active.
events: The backup begins its read transaction.
Before its first snapshot-establishing store read, an accepted owner change commits audit entry 21.
The backup copies, encrypts, checks and keeps the snapshot.
After a store loss, the owner puts that backup in place and starts Registry.
outcomes: Transaction start establishes the snapshot, so the backup excludes entry 21 and records last sequence number 20.
The first store read establishes the snapshot, so the backup includes entry 21 and records last sequence number 21, while its recorded instant remains the earlier transaction-start instant.
basis: A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs: one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot, the instant being when its read transaction began.
An entry is written by an accepted action that changes state and that M09 lists, in the same transaction as the change: if the change is not stored, neither is the entry, and the reverse.
It has no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its place on the host, outside Registry (Explicit exclusions), and Registry starts on it as on any store.

provenance.quote: It has no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its place on the host, outside Registry

topics.topic: Whether AgentSession records are excluded from backup contents
questions: Does the statement that a backup holds whatever the snapshot contains have an exception for AgentSession records, or must those records remain in the backup?

judgement.why: P3 already judged the same backup-session question on unchanged text, and the later flow expressly removes agent sessions from the copied snapshot.

precedent.topic: Whether backup snapshots include or exclude agent-session records
quotes:
`capability:store.copy_store_snapshot` writes one
read snapshot of the store, the agent sessions removed, at the temporary
path `module:backups` named, and answers that transaction's start instant
and the last sequence number the audit counter holds (A18 rules 1, 2,
A15 rule 5).
precedent.why: State 4 expressly defines the copied snapshot as the store snapshot with agent sessions removed.

topics.topic: Whether the A18 amendment reopens A21 security review
questions: Does this A18 change leave A21 reopened, or is the existing performed-again statement intended to certify the changed rules too?

judgement.why: P2 already judged the same review-reopening question from the unchanged performed-again passage, which states that A18 reopened A21 and was reviewed again.

precedent.topic: Whether the A18 change reopens the A21 security review
quotes:
Performed again on 2026-11-01, after that day's changes to A01, A04, A13, A16,
A17 and A18 reopened it (rule 2): every category naming them was reviewed, and no
outcome changed; concurrency now names A18 too, whose one-snapshot copy and
non-overlapping runs (rule 1) it relies on.
precedent.why: The text expressly says the A18 change reopened the review and that every affected category was reviewed again, so the recorded PERFORMED result is the post-change result.
